problem.question: Is this really a problem today?
problem.answer: Yes! It’s a massive problem, but most Christians are completely unaware of it because they have a Bible or have access to one they can read online. Because it is so easy to read a Bible online, the assumption is that the Bible must be easy to use and share, right? But anyone who has tried to get access to Scripture to *make* something (an app, a website, a new Bible translation, an audio Bible, etc.) knows that is not the case. And for a world that desperately needs the gospel, this is completely inexcusable.

attribution.question: What’s wrong with requiring others to attribute the creator of a Bible translation?
attribution.answer: Requesting attribution is not necessarily a problem, but *requiring it* as a condition to distribute the Bible certainly is.

money.question: But how do Bible translators and publishers make money?

nonCommercial.question: What’s wrong with requiring noncommercial use?
nonCommercial.answer: It is wrong to put **any** restrictions on others when it comes to freely distributing or sharing Scripture, full stop. There are many ways a Bible could be distributed commercially in a pure and faithful manner (for example, printing Bibles and selling them at just the price required to make a small profit to reinvest in the operation and increase distribution). The point, dear Christian, is that it is *not your place* to tell others how they can and cannot use God’s word.

compare.caption: What the Free Use Bible API and three widely used Bible APIs let you do

ours.permission: Nothing to accept. AO Lab adds no restrictions; each text keeps its own notice
ours.storage: Cache, store and download without expiry

apiBible.permission: Accept API.Bible’s terms; commercial use adds a licence for each translation
apiBible.storage: Cache allowed, but must refresh at least every 30 days
apiBible.openSource: Client SDKs are open source; the API itself is not

youVersion.permission: Accept the platform terms, then a publisher agreement for each set of translations
youVersion.storage: Set by each publisher agreement; some allow in-app offline use, some limit how much is shown at once
youVersion.openSource: Client SDKs are open source; the API itself is not

bibleBrain.account: Key required, granted at their discretion
bibleBrain.usage: None published, and access can be limited or revoked at any time
bibleBrain.permission: Accept the licence; keys are approved at their discretion
bibleBrain.storage: Offline use only via their download endpoint

compare.storageNote: *Copy and store on your own hardware, servers, or on a device so it works offline.
